Day 1
From Hotel: 11 min · 3 min → Kapuzinerberg
1. Kapuzinerberg
A forested hill rising directly above the Salzach — stone steps climb past 17th-century fortification walls and the Capuchin Monastery to the Hettwer Bastei, a wide terrace with an uninterrupted view over the Altstadt rooftops to the Hohensalzburg Fortress and the Alps.
Read more
Daily 7:00am - 9:00pm
~1.5 hr
Free
The Hettwer Bastei terrace is the viewpoint — reached by the stepped Imbergsteige from Steingasse, a steady 15-minute climb.
Imbergsteige · Neustadt
14 min · 4 min → Hohensalzburg Fortress
2. Hohensalzburg Fortress
One of the largest fully preserved medieval fortresses in Europe, crowning the Festungsberg above the old town; the FestungsBahn funicular carries you up to ramparts, state rooms and sweeping views.
Read more
Hohensalzburg Fortress · 4.6 · festung-hohensalzburg.at
Daily 8:30am - 8:00pm
~2 hr
May - September hours for the grounds; the museums, Prince’s Rooms and Magic Theatre run 9:00am - 7:00pm. The FestungsBahn funicular from Festungsgasse is included in the all-inclusive ticket.
Festungsgasse 4 · Festungsberg
1 min · 3 min → St. Peter's Abbey & Catacombs
3. St. Peter's Abbey & Catacombs
Founded around 696, the oldest monastery in the German-speaking world; its catacombs are hewn into the Mönchsberg cliff above a baroque cemetery of wrought-iron crosses and arcades.
Read more
St. Peter's Catacombs · 3.9 · stift-stpeter.at
Daily 10:00am - 12:30pm · 1:00pm - 6:00pm
~45 min
Cash Only
Sankt-Peter-Bezirk 1 · Altstadt
4 min · 4 min → DomQuartier Salzburg
4. DomQuartier Salzburg
A single grand circuit through the Prince-Archbishops' Residenz state rooms, the cathedral's organ gallery and arcade terraces, and the abbey's art collections — baroque Salzburg's seat of power, all under one ticket.
Read more
DomQuartier Salzburg · 4.6 · domquartier.at
Daily 10:00am - 6:00pm
~2 hr
July and August hours; the rest of the year 10:00am - 5:00pm and closed Tuesday. Last admission one hour before closing.
Residenzplatz 1 · Altstadt
12 min · 5 min → Nonnberg Abbey
5. Nonnberg Abbey
Founded around 714 AD and still an active Benedictine community, this is the oldest continuously occupied convent north of the Alps — the Romanesque church with its gilded Gothic altar, the graveyard and the terrace above the Altstadt rooftops are open to visitors.
Read more
Daily 6:45am - 7:00pm
~1 hr
Free
Nonnberggasse 2 · Festungsberg

Day 2
From Hotel: 12 min → Hellbrunn Palace & Trick Fountains
1. Hellbrunn Palace & Trick Fountains
A 1615 prince-archbishop's summer villa built for play — hidden water jets soak the unwary, a water-powered mechanical theatre turns 200 figures, and grottoes still ambush visitors four centuries on.
Read more
Hellbrunn Trick Fountains · 4.6 · hellbrunn.at
Daily 9:30am - 6:30pm
~2 hr
Fürstenweg 37 · Hellbrunn
11 min · 1 min → Salzburg Zoo Hellbrunn
2. Salzburg Zoo Hellbrunn
Fourteen hectares of open valley enclosures pressed against the Hellbrunn cliff — white rhinoceros, snow leopards, jaguars and a free-flight alpine ibex range, with the rock face itself forming the boundary of the big-cat and vulture enclosures; around 1,500 animals share the site with the palace park next door.
Read more
Salzburg Zoo Hellbrunn · 4.6 · salzburg-zoo.at
Daily 9:00am - 6:00pm
~2.5 hr
August hours; last admission 5:00pm. A combined Zoo + Hellbrunn Palace ticket is sold at either gate. Night Zoo runs every Friday and Saturday in August.
Hellbrunner Straße 60 · Anif
12 min → hotel
Day 3
From Hotel: 9 min · 4 min → Mozart's Residence
1. Mozart's Residence
The spacious apartment on the Makartplatz where the family lived from 1773 — original fortepianos, letters in Mozart's hand and the Sound & Film Museum show how the composer's work spread from Salzburg to the world.
Read more
Mozart's Residence · 4.4 · mozarteum.at
Daily 9:00am - 5:30pm
~1 hr
Combined ticket with Mozart's Birthplace available at shop.mozarteum.at.
Makartplatz 8 · Neustadt
5 min · 1 min → Mirabell Palace & Gardens
2. Mirabell Palace & Gardens
Baroque pleasure gardens laid out in 1690 — the flowered parterre, Pegasus fountain and Grand Staircase frame a postcard view of the fortress, and the steps and arbours feature in The Sound of Music.
Read more
Daily 6:00am - 8:00pm
~1 hr
Mirabellplatz · Neustadt
11 min · 3 min → Mozart's Birthplace
3. Mozart's Birthplace
The yellow house at Getreidegasse 9 where Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart was born on 27 January 1756 — six rooms display his childhood violin, family portraits, original scores and the keyboard he played as a prodigy of five.
Read more
Mozart's Birthplace · 4.4 · mozarteum.at
Daily 9:00am - 5:30pm
~1 hr
Last admission 30 min before closing. The combined ticket with Mozart’s Residence is the cheaper option if you are doing both.
Getreidegasse 9 · Altstadt
6 min · 1 min → Haus der Natur
4. Haus der Natur
One of Austria's top natural history museums — 80 exhibition rooms across 7,300 sq m: a life-sized moving Allosaurus, an aquarium with forty tanks of exotic fish and reptiles, a whale skeleton in the palaeontology wing, a space hall, and a three-floor Science Center.
Haus der Natur · 4.7 · hausdernatur.at
Daily 9:00am - 5:00pm
~3 hr
Last entry 4:30pm.
Museumsplatz 5 · Altstadt
1 min · 1 min → Museum der Moderne Mönchsberg
5. Museum der Moderne Mönchsberg
A clifftop gallery clad in fine-grained Untersberg marble, reached by a glass-walled lift from the Altstadt — the permanent collection and rotating international exhibitions hang above a panoramic terrace with a sweeping view of the city.
Read more
Museum der Moderne Mönchsberg · 4.3 · museumdermoderne.at
Tuesday - Sunday 10:00am - 6:00pm · Thursday 10:00am - 8:00pm
Closed Monday
~1.5 hr
Reached via the Mönchsbergaufzug lift at Gstättengasse 13 — elevator ticket included with museum admission.
Mönchsberg 32 · Mönchsberg

Day 4
From Hotel: 18 min → Untersberg
1. Untersberg
A cable car climbs from St. Leonhard to the 1,776 m Geiereck summit in under nine minutes, opening a panorama over Salzburg, the Salzkammergut lakes and the peaks of Berchtesgaden.
Read more
Untersbergbahn Cable Car · 4.8 · untersbergbahn.at
Daily 8:30am - 5:30pm
~2 hr
May 1 - September 30 hours; cars run every 30 min. Last ride up 5:00pm, last ride down 5:30pm. Bring a layer — the summit is markedly cooler than the valley.
Dr.-Friedrich-Oedl-Weg 2 · Grödig
13 min → Salzwelten Hallein Salt Mine
2. Salzwelten Hallein Salt Mine
An underground world of shimmering salt galleries beneath the Dürrnberg plateau — the guided tour takes you through tunnels by wooden mine slide, crosses a briny underground lake by boat and tells the story of the Celtic salt trade that made Salzburg rich.
Read more
Salzwelten Salt Mine Entry · 4.8 · 730+ reviews — GetYourGuide
Daily 9:00am - 5:00pm
~2 hr
Season March 28 - November 1. The last guided tour departs at 5:00pm. Overalls are provided; the tour includes two wooden miners’ slides and a boat crossing of the underground salt lake.
Ramsaustraße 3 · Bad Dürrnberg
26 min → hotel
Day 5
From Hotel: 11 min → Hangar-7
1. Hangar-7
Red Bull's aviation and racing museum at Salzburg Airport — the glass-and-steel hangar houses historic aircraft from inter-war biplanes to Cold War jets alongside Formula 1 cars and World Rally Championship vehicles; admission is free and the terrace overlooks the apron.
Read more
Monday - Saturday 9:00am - 10:00pm · Sunday 9:00am - 5:00pm
~1.5 hr
Free
Wilhelm-Spazier-Straße 7A · Airport
5 min → Stiegl-Brauwelt
2. Stiegl-Brauwelt
Austria's largest private brewery opens 5,000 sq m of itself to visitors — a 270-degree cinema, the world's tallest beer tower, the malt and hop rooms, and a walk along the working production route, closing at a tasting bar where the day's brews are poured beneath the copper kettles.
Read more
Stiegl-Brauwelt · 4.4 · brauwelt.at
Daily 10:00am - 7:00pm
~2 hr
Museum entry is self-guided. Guided brewery tours with the production route and a tasting run daily at 10:30am, 1:00pm and 3:30pm — the 1:00pm departure is the English-language one.
Bräuhausstraße 9 · Maxglan

1. Goldenes Dachl
Built in 1497 for Emperor Maximilian I, this gilded oriel of 2,657 fire-gilded copper tiles juts over Herzog-Friedrich-Straße — the Innsbruck Museum inside the balcony tells the Habsburg story, while the glittering canopy above is one of Austria's most recognisable medieval landmarks.

2. Hofburg Innsbruck
An alpine Habsburg palace rebuilt on Maria Theresa's orders in the 1770s — the White Hall is one of the grandest Rococo rooms in Austria, and the Imperial Apartments are hung with full-length portraits of her sixteen children arranged in order of birth.
Read more

ARRIVE Werfen Bahnhof: 11 min → Eisriesenwelt
1. Eisriesenwelt Ice Caves
The world's largest accessible system of ice caves — 42 km of passages carved into the Tennengebirge by meltwater, where a guided tour by magnesium lamp leads through vaulted chambers of ice columns, frozen waterfalls and the vast ice cathedral of the Alexander Mörk-Dom.
Read more
Eisriesenwelt · 4.5 · eisriesenwelt.at
Daily 9:30am - 3:45pm
~4 hr
Season May 1 - November 1. The ticket desk shuts at 3:00pm, the cable car at 3:20pm and the last cave tour leaves at 3:45pm — arrive by early afternoon. The combi ticket is cheaper booked online than at the desk and skips the queue. From Werfen Bahnhof: shuttle bus to the cable car base station, cable car to the Bergstation, then a 20-min walk to the cave entrance. The cave stays below freezing all year — bring a warm layer and grippy shoes.
Eishöhlenstraße 30 · Werfen
13 min → Hohenwerfen Fortress
2. Hohenwerfen Fortress
A 900-year-old rock fortress on a wooded cone above the Salzach, ringed by the Tennengebirge — the castle tour climbs through the bell tower and armoury, and the falconers of Europe's oldest working falconry centre fly eagles, vultures and falcons from the lower courtyard against the valley below.
Read more
Hohenwerfen Fortress · 4.6 · burg-hohenwerfen.at
Daily 9:00am - 5:00pm
~2.5 hr
July 20 - August 21 opens to 6:00pm. Birds of prey demonstrations 11:15am and 3:15pm — plus 2:15pm and 4:30pm from July 20 to August 21. Castle interior is by guided tour only, 50 min, included in the ticket. Season April 1 - November 2.

2. Schönbrunn Palace
The Habsburg summer residence in imperial yellow — 1,441 rooms with state apartments where Mozart played at age six, Marie Antoinette grew up and Franz Joseph I died; the Grand Parterre gardens climb to a hilltop Gloriette with the best panorama of Vienna.

ARRIVE Berchtesgaden Hbf: 15 min → Königssee
1. Königssee
Bavaria's most pristine glacial lake, set entirely within Berchtesgaden National Park — electric-powered boats glide across the emerald water to the onion-domed St. Bartholomä church on the western shore, where the boatman demonstrates the natural echo off the canyon walls with a trumpet call.
Read more
Königssee Boat Tickets · 4.8 · seenschifffahrt.de
Daily 8:00am - 5:30pm
~2.5 hr
Season April 25 - October 11. Boats run every 30 min from Seelände dock. Arrive early — queues build quickly in peak season.
Seestraße 55 · Schönau am Königssee
50 min → Kehlsteinhaus
2. Kehlsteinhaus · Eagle's Nest
Hitler's Alpine retreat at 1,834 m above Berchtesgaden — reached by the original 1938 mountain road and a 124 m elevator bored into the Kehlstein rock; the summit terrace opens a panorama over the Berchtesgaden Alps into Austria, and the historic rooms now house a restaurant.
Read more
Kehlsteinhaus Bus Pass · 4.6 · kehlsteinhaus.axess.shop
Daily 8:30am - 5:00pm
~2 hr
Season mid-May to late October. The bus ticket — elevator included — is compulsory; no private car may use the Kehlsteinstraße. Buy online or at the Dokumentation Obersalzberg terminal. Bus RVO 849 departs every 25 min; last return 5:00pm.

Local Tastes
Salzburger Nockerl
A cloud-light baked soufflé of whipped egg whites in three peaks, dusted with sugar to mimic the city's hills — sweet, warm and meant to be shared.
St. Peter Stiftskulinarium · Zum Eulenspiegel
Original Salzburger Mozartkugel
A hand-rolled sphere of pistachio marzipan and nougat dipped in dark chocolate, invented by Paul Fürst in 1890 and still made by hand to the original recipe.
Café-Konditorei Fürst
Bosna
Salzburg's own street-food sausage — bratwurst in a griddled white roll with onions, parsley and a curry-spiced mustard, born at the Balkan Grill on Getreidegasse.
Balkan Grill Walter
Augustiner Bräu
Monastery-brewed beer poured from wooden kegs into stone steins, drunk in Salzburg's vast Mülln beer garden — a tradition running since 1621.
Augustiner Bräustübl

Day Trips by Train
Linz · 1 hr 10 min
Upper Austria's third city — the Lentos Museum of modern art on the Danube, the vast Ars Electronica Center on digital culture, and the old city around Hauptplatz. Fast Railjet trains run direct on the Westbahn corridor.
book at: oebb.at or Omio
Bad Ischl · 1 hr 20 min
Emperor Franz Joseph's summer retreat on the Traun river — the Kaiservilla where he hunted for 60 summers, the Imperial Salt Spa and the lakeside market town that anchors the Salzkammergut; change at Attnang-Puchheim.
book at: oebb.at or Omio
Kufstein · 1 hr 20 min
Tyrolean market town on the Inn River dominated by a medieval hilltop fortress — the Heldenorgel is the world's largest outdoor pipe organ, 4,948 pipes bored into the Bürgerturm, playing a daily noon concert; also a military history museum, cobblestone old town, and alpine views into Bavaria.
book at: oebb.at or Omio
Munich · 1 hr 30 min
Bavaria's capital across the border — Marienplatz, the Residenz and the English Garden; direct regional and EuroCity trains run there in 1 hr 30 min.
book at: oebb.at or Omio
Hallstatt · 2 hr 35 min
Storybook lakeside village of pastel houses below alpine cliffs; the train runs to a pier where a short ferry crosses the Hallstättersee to the old town, changing at Attnang-Puchheim.
book at: oebb.at or Omio

Packing for Hiking
Worth Knowing

Salzburg rewards looking up. The fortress watches the whole city, the Mönchsberg and Untersberg ring it in green and grey, and from the Mirabell parterre the castle lines up perfectly above the flowerbeds.

The city itself is small and the hotel sits on the Neustadt side of the river, so Days 1, 3 and 5 are walkable and the Altstadt is fifteen minutes away on foot over the Staatsbrücke. Everything south and east — Hellbrunn, the Untersberg, the salt mine, the ice caves — is a car ride, and the days are built that way.

Time each day around the light. The Altstadt is at its best before ten, when the day-trip coaches have not yet emptied onto Getreidegasse; the south — Hellbrunn's water gardens and the Untersberg summit — holds the long afternoon. Carry cash for St. Peter's catacombs, expect to be soaked at the trick fountains, and book Eisriesenwelt and the Kehlstein bus online the night before: both sell out in August and both stop selling long before they close.
